planning_policy.source: Anubis guided-1.0 planning defaults, consultant accepted; not measured

reference_assumptions.source: Fictional consultant planning assumption for this demonstration, not measured benchmark evidence. 12,000 independent images in four hours. Fixed diffusion model, 1024 square, 30 steps, BF16. Each capacity is for a complete eight-GPU group.

sections.text: A conditional planning estimate is available. It depends on the accepted assumptions and is not a guarantee of production performance. Treat this as an early planning view for discussion, not a committed build promise. Check assumptions with the architect before relying on it.

The workload estimate is 24 GPUs. The selected factory deployment anchor is 256 GPUs. These are different quantities. HGX_B300: 24 estimated GPUs (sensitivity 16 to 24). HGX_B200: 24 estimated GPUs (sensitivity 24 to 32). HGX_H200: 40 estimated GPUs (sensitivity 32 to 48). Counts use whole GPU nodes. Spare compute does not establish an admitted tenant count. Sensitivity is not a confidence interval. The estimate reflects workload size while the chosen factory size is larger. Extra room remains available but does not by itself mean ready customers can be added.

Required memory per GPU: 80 GB. Selected hardware memory per GPU: 288 GB. Host RAM provision for the workload: 6144 GB. Host local disk provision: 92160 GB. Host provisions are planning assumptions. Per-device memory fit matters, not just aggregate memory. Working memory per graphics processor is the key fit question, not just total memory across the factory. Host memory and local disk figures are planning assumptions to review with the architect.

No local shared-storage capacity has been established. This is not a zero-storage requirement. An outside corpus is not automatically copied into this factory. Shared storage for the factory is not yet settled, and this does not mean no storage is needed. Outside data does not appear automatically and must be brought in separately.

External customer datacenter ingress: unresolved. North-south ingress: unresolved. Dedicated storage read/write links: unresolved / unresolved. East-west link per GPU: unresolved. Storage networking is physically dedicated, not converged. External and north-south rates describe the same traffic at different boundaries and must not be added together. These are lower bounds, not selected circuit sizes. Traffic entering the factory and communication between GPUs remain open questions. The stated rates are lower bounds rather than final circuit choices.

East-west per-GPU port demand needs the selected reference design and collective-communication measurements. Customer-datacenter round-trip latency objective is unspecified.
